PullRequest.Title: adding option to make cmd+d be case sensitive or case insensitive
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Add the `editor.selectionMatchCase` option to control case sensitivity for selection occurrences independently of the Find widget.
- Apply the option to Add Next/Previous Occurrence, Move to Next/Previous Occurrence, Select All Occurrences, and selection highlighting.
- Preserve existing behavior for caret-started occurrence selection, which remains whole-word and case-sensitive, while Find-focused commands continue to use the Find widget options.

## Manual verification

```
foo
foobar
FOO
FOOBAR
```

- [x] With the default `editor.selectionMatchCase: false`, select `foo` and press Cmd+D; verify that `foo`, `FOO`, and substring occurrences such as `fooBar` can be selected.
- [x] Set `editor.selectionMatchCase` to `true`, select `foo`, and press Cmd+D; verify that differently cased occurrences such as `FOO` are skipped while same-case substring occurrences are still selected.
- [x] Place the caret inside a word without selecting text and press Cmd+D; verify that matching remains whole-word and case-sensitive regardless of the setting.
- [x] Open and focus the Find widget with Match Case and Match Whole Word configured differently from `editor.selectionMatchCase`; search for something in the Find widget and verify that the Find widget options are honored.
- [x] Select text in the editor and verify that occurrence highlights follow `editor.selectionMatchCase`, including after toggling the setting.
- [x] Verify Add Previous Occurrence, Move to Next/Previous Occurrence, and Select All Occurrences follow the same case-sensitivity rules as Cmd+D.

## Limitations

Currently there is no setting for selection whole word matching, only a setting for case sensitivity. This should probably also be added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor-focused Add Next/Previous or Move Next/Previous Occurrence from a selection or caret (for example Cmd+D)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The keybinding synchronously determines whether Find owns the request, reuses or creates a MultiCursorSession, then performs one in-memory text-model findNextMatch/findPreviousMatch before updating and revealing selections. The diff adds only constant-time focus/state/option reads and can avoid the prior hidden Find-options UI highlighting; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search cost scales with text traversed to the next/previous match; selection-array copying scales with the number of existing cursors. Case-insensitive mode can increase matches reached, but the default Find state was already case-insensitive and each incremental command still performs one search.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the editor input path: one model search per command invocation; repeated commands reuse one session until selection, model, blur, or ownership changes end it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The MultiCursorSession caches query text and matching flags for the sequence, not search results. Focus ownership changes intentionally invalidate the session. There is no negative-cache behavior or concurrent request to coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed calls and model-search path are directly visible, and all work remains in-process and synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact model-search latency varies with document size and query, but the diff does not increase search cardinality or concurrency on the normal default path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new option substitutes a constant-time option read for Find-state settings and the ownership guard avoids irrelevant Find-options UI work for editor-driven selection.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command synchronously checks text focus and revealed/non-empty Find state, then uses the existing Find query and performs one local model search (findNext/findPrevious or findMatches for select-all) before setting selections. No external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Navigation scales with text scanned to the next match. Select-all scales with document size and effective match count, with the existing MAX_SAFE_SMALL_INTEGER result limit unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized in the UI command handler, with one model search per navigation command or one full search for select-all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A session is reused while Find retains ownership; crossing focus ownership clears it. No remote/cache boundary exists, and no new retries are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete selectAll and session call paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very match-dense documents can already create many selections, but the diff neither removes the existing limit nor adds a second scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new drivenByFind routing preserves one-search behavior and only recreates a session when ownership changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selection occurrence highlighting after selection, model content, Find state, or selectionMatchCase configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection changes may update immediately; model content uses the existing 300 ms RunOnceScheduler; changing the new option schedules one coalesced zero-delay update. The update creates/reuses SelectionHighlighterState, performs at most one in-memory full-model findMatches on a cache miss, filters matches, allocates decoration descriptors, and updates the decoration collection. Large-tokenization models retain the existing early exit. No external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: On a cache miss, CPU/allocation scales with document text and effective occurrence count; decoration work scales with matches. Case sensitivity may change effective cardinality by intended semantics, while the default false matches the pre-diff default Find state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI-thread serialized. RunOnceScheduler coalesces repeated configuration schedules; there are no parallel searches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SelectionHighlighterState reuses matches when model identity/version, search text, case mode, and word separators are unchanged. A selectionMatchCase toggle changes the cache key and correctly triggers one recomputation; warm unchanged updates reuse cached matches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the scheduler, cache-key, model-size guard, findMatches, and decoration paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Match density determines decoration count, but option toggles are infrequent and the changed scheduling is coalesced rather than per event burst.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only new work is one necessary, coalesced refresh when the matching option itself changes; normal selection highlighting retains its existing scan and allocation structure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor option registration and Monaco/standalone API exposure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor startup/configuration constructs one additional boolean option descriptor and exposes its enum/type declarations. This is constant startup work with no changed transitive I/O or network boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per editor option registry, independent of document size, editor events, or number of matches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous registration during module initialization; no fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved option value follows the existing editor configuration cache/event mechanism; no new standalone cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the option registration and declaration-only hunks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible constant metadata size; no scaling mechanism is present.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and every diff page. Traced occurrence navigation, select-all, focus ownership/session lifecycle, selection-highlighter scans/cache/decorations, and option startup registration. The change adds no external boundary fan-out, concurrency burst, unbounded retention, or repeated hot-path work; no valid performance finding or regression-fix record was established.
